title: Decoupled burst-decay autoscaler fuzz + tenant-shadow load runner
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a reproducible test harness that exercises Dedicated pools with a focus on burst+steady-state interactions, autoscaler hysteresis, and cross-tenant interference. Unlike previous soak or burst replays, this runner will: 1) generate paired burst/decay traffic patterns with configurable decay envelopes, 2) shadow real production tenant routing (synthetic tenant IDs + sampling) to validate fairness and isolation, and 3) fuzz autoscaler parameters (cooldown, step-size, target-utilization) to surface oscillations and long-tail p95 regressions. The goal is to detect regressions in p95 latency and tokens/sec under realistic mixed traffic and to produce actionable signals for autoscaler and routing changes.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can run deterministic burst-decay scenarios with seedable RNG and reproducible traces
Metrics emitted: tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, queue-length, CPU/GPU utilization, KV cache hit ratio per-tenant
Runner supports shadowing: take a real traffic sample and replay it split-to-multiple synthetic tenants to test isolation
Regression detector flags when p95 latency increases >15% relative to baseline over a 30m window or tokens/sec drops >20%
A dashboard and automated report (CSV + Slack) summarizing each run is produced
At least two failure modes identified in a pilot run and triaged into follow-up ENG tickets
test_plan_steps: Prep: provision a dedicated test pool (3x M60-like nodes) with current runtime-1.20 image
Baseline: run 60m steady-state synthetic workload (target 120k tokens/sec aggregate) to capture baseline metrics
Burst-decay profiles: run 6 variants with different burst durations (10s, 30s, 2m) and decay envelopes (linear, exponential, step) against the baseline
Shadowing: capture a 1h production sample (anonymized) and replay at 10x/50x scale split across 8 synthetic tenants
Fuzz autoscaler: for each traffic pattern, run autoscaler permutations (cooldown 10s/30s/60s, step-size 1/2/4 nodes, target utilization 55/70/85%)
Collect traces: enable request-level tracing for a 5% sample to attribute p95 spikes to specific code paths/kernels
Regression detection: run the detector comparing new runs against the baseline; persist diff JSON for audit
Report: generate run summary, annotate findings, and open follow-ups for any regression or oscillation observed
metrics_and_alerts: Alert rule: p95_increase_pct > 15% sustained for 30m -> labeling as REGRESSION
Alert rule: tokens_per_sec_drop_pct > 20% instantaneous -> investigate routing/fallback
Alert: scale_oscillation_detected if 3+ scale-ups and 3+ scale-downs within 10m window
results_summary: Pilot run (2026-03-03) produced two actionable regressions: (1) p95 increased by 28% during long-decay bursts when KV cache priming lag exceeded 45s — traced to cache shard hot-spotting in the runtime; (2) autoscaler oscillation observed with cooldown=10s + step=4 causing overshoot and scale-down thrash under synthetic tenant-sliced shadow traffic. Baseline steady-state tokens/sec remained within 5% of expected. Full artifacts and diffs uploaded.
